title: "3. Figures"

This script draws the plots: the observed weekly series, the exploratory models, and the article's two figures. It saves the figures to `figures/`, which is not in the repository, because they are made from the study data. The published figures are on the published results page.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/figures.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COVID-infection-control/blob/main/R/figures.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COVID-infection-control/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COVID-infection-control/blob/main/R/functions.R)
-   [`R/prepare_data.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COVID-infection-control/blob/main/R/prepare_data.R)
-   [`R/models.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COVID-infection-control/blob/main/R/models.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/figures.R")
```

## The observed series

The first look at the data, before any model: each week's percentage positive and HAI rate, with their 95% intervals, and a red line at the intervention. Every week-based plot is drawn by [`plot_weekly_series()`](functions.qmd#plotting-a-weekly-series).

```{r}
#| label: plot-observed-series
#| eval: false
```

## The exploratory models

Each exploratory model's fitted line over the observed series. Laid side by side with Figure 1, they show what each simpler model misses: a single trend cannot follow the rise and fall, a level change alone ignores the trend, and a level change with one shared trend cannot bend after the intervention. These plots were not in the article.

```{r}
#| label: plot-exploratory-models
#| eval: false
```

## Figure 1

The published model for both outcomes: panel A, test positivity; panel B, the HAI rate. The blue line is the segmented regression, rising until week 12, stepping down at the intervention, and then falling.

The size legend of panel A reads "# patients tested", as in the original code, although the points are sized by the number of healthcare-personnel tests.

```{r}
#| label: plot-figure-1
#| eval: false
```

## Figure 2: lines by date

Figure 2 plots the same series by date rather than by week, so the hospital data can be set against daily Harris County cases. As in the original code, its fitted line joins the published model's predictions at the observed weeks, so it does not show Figure 1's step at the intervention.

```{r}
#| label: prepare-figure-2-lines
#| eval: false
```

## Figure 2

Each panel shows a hospital series with daily Harris County cases as grey bars behind it, on a second axis to the right. The comparison is the point of the figure: infections in the hospital fell more quickly than cases in the community, which the article notes when discussing whether the fall only reflected the community wave.

```{r}
#| label: plot-figure-2
#| eval: false
```

## Saving the figures

The figures are saved as TIFF files in `figures/`. As in the original code, no size is set, so `ggsave()` uses the size of the current graphics device.

```{r}
#| label: save-figures
#| eval: false
```
